title: Right tension pneumothorax after blunt trauma

card.complaint: Motorcyclist with a chest injury, rapidly worsening breathlessness

triage.note: Motorcycle versus car at about 50 km/h, helmeted. Struck the right side of his chest on the handlebar. Paramedics gave oxygen by face mask. Increasingly breathless over the last 10 minutes.

speech.impairedText: (Too breathless to answer. He grips your arm.)

appearance.text: Breathing more easily and talking in sentences. Colour improving.
Breathless but talking in short sentences.
Severely distressed, sitting up, speaking in single words. Lips dusky.
Agitated, then drowsy. Gasping and grey.

history.q: Ask the paramedic for a handover
history.a: MIST: motorcycle versus car, about 50 km/h, helmet on, no loss of consciousness. Injury to the right chest wall. On scene HR 110, BP 118/76, RR 26, SpO₂ 94%, getting worse en route. Oxygen by face mask. We couldn’t get IV access.
Bike… car hit me… chest… handlebar.
Can’t… get air. Worse… and worse.

history.q: Any pain in your head, neck, tummy or legs?

exam.label: Airway
exam.text: Talking in short phrases. Airway patent, no stridor.

exam.label: Trachea & neck veins
exam.text: Trachea deviated to the LEFT. Neck veins distended.

variants.text: Trachea central. Neck veins no longer distended.

exam.label: Chest
exam.text: Bruising over the right lateral chest wall. Reduced expansion, hyper-resonant percussion and absent breath sounds on the right. Left side normal.

variants.text: Bruising over the right lateral chest wall. Breath sounds returning on the right, less resonant. Left side normal.

exam.label: Circulation
exam.text: Rapid, thready pulse. Capillary refill 4 s. Heart sounds normal.

exam.label: Abdomen & pelvis
exam.text: Soft, non-tender, no bruising. Pelvis not examined by springing (binder not indicated).

exam.label: Disability
exam.text: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6). Pupils equal and reactive. Moving all four limbs.

exam.label: Exposure
exam.text: Abrasions to the right arm. No long-bone deformity.

investigations.label: eFAST ultrasound
investigations.text: Right: absent lung sliding, barcode sign on M-mode. Left: lung sliding present. No pericardial effusion. No free fluid in the abdomen.

variants.text: Right: lung sliding partly visible anteriorly. Left: normal. No pericardial effusion. No free fluid.

investigations.label: Venous blood gas
investigations.text: pH 7.28, pCO₂ 55 mmHg, lactate 4.1 mmol/L, Hb 13.9 g/dL.

investigations.label: Trauma bloods, group & crossmatch
investigations.text: Hb 13.6 g/dL, platelets 210 ×10⁹/L, INR 1.0. Group O RhD positive; 2 units crossmatched.

investigations.label: Chest X-ray (portable)
investigations.text: Large right pneumothorax with mediastinal shift to the left and a flattened right hemidiaphragm.

variants.text: Right chest drain in situ; lung re-expanded. Undisplaced fractures of the right 5th and 6th ribs. Mediastinum central.
Right pneumothorax, smaller; decompression device in situ. Mediastinum central.

investigations.label: CT chest (trauma series)
investigations.text: Right chest drain in situ, small residual pneumothorax, undisplaced right 5th–6th rib fractures, small lung contusion. No other injury.

variants.text: Radiographer: “He’s too unstable to come to CT. Stabilise him first.”

interventions.label: IV access
interventions.detail: Two large-bore cannulae (IO if not possible)

interventions.label: Needle decompression, RIGHT
interventions.detail: 4th/5th ICS just anterior to mid-axillary line (or 2nd ICS MCL)
interventions.say: A hiss of air on insertion.

interventions.label: Needle decompression, LEFT
interventions.detail: 4th/5th ICS just anterior to mid-axillary line

harm.why: Wrong side. Decompressing the normal side creates a pneumothorax in the good lung.

interventions.label: Finger thoracostomy, RIGHT
interventions.detail: 4th/5th ICS, just anterior to mid-axillary line
interventions.say: A rush of air through the thoracostomy.

interventions.label: Chest drain (ICD), RIGHT
interventions.say: Nurse: “Drain in. It’s swinging and bubbling.”

interventions.label: RSI and intubation
interventions.feedback: Positive-pressure ventilation can turn a simple pneumothorax into a tension pneumothorax. Decompress first, and have a chest drain in place when ventilating.

interventions.label: Transfuse O-negative blood
interventions.feedback: Nothing suggested haemorrhage: this shock was obstructive. Blood carries its own risks.

dispositions.label: Admit under trauma surgery (HDU) with chest drain; CT once stable
Straight to CT now, then decide

critical.label: Right chest decompressed
critical.why: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. Decompress immediately, before imaging.

critical.label: Chest drain inserted
critical.why: Needle decompression is temporary. A chest drain is the definitive treatment.

recommended.label: Examined chest, trachea and neck veins

penalties.why: A chest X-ray was requested before decompression. Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis; imaging delays life-saving treatment.
Intubated before decompressing the chest. Positive-pressure ventilation worsens tension physiology and can precipitate arrest.
CT was requested while the patient was hypotensive. Unstable patients go to CT only after stabilisation.

teaching: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis: respiratory distress, hypoxia, tachycardia and hypotension with unilateral absent breath sounds and hyper-resonance. Tracheal deviation and distended neck veins are late and unreliable signs.
Decompress immediately. Do not wait for a chest X-ray.

ATLS (10th edition) recommends needle decompression in adults at the 4th/5th intercostal space just anterior to the mid-axillary line, where the chest wall is thinner. The 2nd intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line is still used in children and some systems.
Needles kink, block and fall short. Reassess after decompression. Finger thoracostomy is preferred in ventilated or arrested patients. Follow with a chest drain.
Positive-pressure ventilation can turn a simple pneumothorax into a tension pneumothorax.
In traumatic cardiac arrest, treat reversible causes (hypoxia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, hypovolaemia) before adrenaline.
references: American College of Surgeons. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS), 10th edition (2018).
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: cardiac arrest in special circumstances (traumatic cardiac arrest).
